result.summary: The image depicts a wide, car-centric arterial road with multiple travel lanes and a painted center turn lane. Pedestrian infrastructure is largely absent, with no visible sidewalks or marked crosswalks, forcing pedestrians to navigate unpaved shoulders or parking areas.

hazards.name: Lack of Sidewalks
hazards.description: Pedestrians are forced to walk on unpaved shoulders or in the roadway due to the absence of a continuous paved walkway.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: Despite the presence of a traffic signal, there are no marked crosswalks for pedestrians to safely cross the wide multi-lane road.

hazards.name: Parked Vehicle Obstructions
hazards.description: Vehicles parked on the shoulder block pedestrian paths and create sightline obstructions between drivers and people on foot.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the road and left parking area

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct continuous, ADA-compliant paved sidewalks on both sides of the street to separate pedestrians from vehicle traffic.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks and Pedestrian Signals
interventions.description: Install high-visibility crosswalks and dedicated pedestrian signal heads at the signalized intersection.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Convert the painted center turn lane into a raised pedestrian refuge island at the crossing point to reduce exposure time.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a sidewalk separated from the roadway by a line of parked vehicles, which significantly obstruct sightlines. While a traffic signal is present, there are no visible marked crosswalks or pedestrian-specific signals, creating a gap in safe crossing infrastructure at this intersection.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Large SUVs parked along the curb block the view between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers on the roadway, especially near the intersection.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground, along the right curb line.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crosswalk
hazards.description: No painted crosswalk is visible at the signalized intersection, which may lead to unpredictable pedestrian movements and reduced driver awareness.
hazards.location_in_image: Intersection area near the traffic light pole.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the intersection to improve sightlines for both drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style crosswalk markings to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way and increase visibility.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signals with countdown timers to provide clear information on when it is safe to cross.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a wide multi-lane roadway with a sidewalk on the left and a signalized intersection in the distance. While basic infrastructure like sidewalks and marked crosswalks are present, the wide road geometry and lack of physical buffers suggest a high-speed environment for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Wide Roadway
hazards.description: The wide, open roadway design encourages higher vehicle speeds and increases the time pedestrians are exposed to traffic while crossing.
hazards.location_in_image: Main roadway extending towards the horizon

hazards.name: Lack of Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the roadway with no physical buffer like a planting strip or parked cars to protect pedestrians from moving traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image along the cemetery fence

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the intersection to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Upgrade the standard transverse crosswalk markings to continental or ladder style to increase visibility to approaching motorists.

result.summary: The image shows a wide, multi-lane intersection with significant pedestrian exposure due to long crossing distances and minimal infrastructure. Large transit vehicles parked along the curb create visual obstructions, while existing crosswalk markings appear faded and insufficient for the scale of the roadway.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide roadway requires pedestrians to be exposed to traffic for a long duration without a refuge.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the main roadway

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Large Vehicles
hazards.description: Parked buses on the right side of the image block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image where buses are parked
